executiveSummary: GM0882 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract, and its official 2025 base is coherent: Landgraaf has 36,839 residents, 27 neighbourhoods in three districts, one BAG place, seven BRT settlement labels, one ProRail station, 43 scheduled-transit stop areas and two logical N300 links. Neighbourhood rows differ by only 19 residents (-0.052%) from the municipality control and remain publication-faithful. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Landgraaf is not a major-river municipality: its locally evidenced water mechanisms are rapid runoff down steep dry valleys and officially designated water-conveying roads, mixed-sewer overload, low-lying Rimburg/Op de Hoven and the German-border Worm regional stream. The generic river preset instead emits exactly 1.159687 m from T+12 through T+72, 13,344 affected people-equivalent and 1,018,940.815 deprived person-hours at T+72 without a Worm hydrograph, terrain/rainfall run, defence, footprint, arrival or recession. Pluvial water becomes exact zero at T+48 despite ongoing official Water in Balans works. The earthquake pulse becomes exact zero by T+12 and cannot represent mine-water uplift, subsidence, changing groundwater or sinkholes from former coal mining. Almost every active T+24 hazard reuses one neighbourhood order led by Lauradorp, Waubach, Heistraat, Exdel and Rimburg. The model also omits the Aachen/Herzogenrath rail branch, German road and mutual-aid connections, German drinking-water supply to southern Landgraaf, external acute-care access, wastewater/pump dependencies, facility occupancy and event crowds of up to 70,000 per day. Public data materially improve context, but static registers, project status and timestamped observations do not establish live condition, capacity, topology or restoration. Unknown, NoData and catalogue no-match must never appear as zero, dry, open or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0882 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; full CBS feature retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK data identify GM0882 as Landgraaf in Limburg and report 36,839 residents, 17,769 households, density 1,499/km² and rounded 28% aged 65 or older; the app retains 28.2% age 65+ and 6,608 one-person households.

Twenty-seven neighbourhood rows in three districts sum to 36,820 residents, 19 below the control (-0.052%); households sum to 17,765 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 10,405. Allocation reconciles to 36,839 without rewriting observations.

BAG supplies one designated place, Landgraaf. BRT supplies Hopel, Landgraaf, Nieuwenhagen, Op de Hoven, Rimburg, Schaesberg and Ubach over Worms: five deelkernen, one gehucht and one woonkern. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0.

The generalized app MultiPolygon has 90 coordinate positions, while the fresh full 2025 municipality feature has 877. Home fields cover 27/27 rows; home value, cars, doctor and supermarket fields 26/27; benefits 25/27; district heat and charging 0/27. Suppressed/null fields remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Water in Balans Rimburg/Rimburgerweg, Worm restoration and Watertakenplan 2023–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Water in Balans cooperation update 7 October 2025; current Worm/RWZI project pages and municipal 2023–2027 plan inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Official project evidence says serious rain flooding occurs in Rimburg and along Rimburgerweg. Water descends from urban Landgraaf and higher rural land; the 2021 event caused major damage, and the current programme aims to retain runoff earlier, keep it out of the foul sewer and guide it toward the Worm.

The project area drains toward the Worm but itself contains dry valleys rather than streams. Rimburgerweg and Lindegracht are officially mapped water-conveying roads during extremes; outside extremes the mixed sewer carries drainage. Properties have elevated risk and fail the provincial waterlogging standard.

The Worm rises in Aachener Wald, forms the German boundary at Rimburg and is managed through cooperation with Kreis Heinsberg and other German partners. This is a regional stream/catchment mechanism, not evidence for an unselected major-river scalar.

Landgraaf's 2023–2027 plan calls climate resilience its principal priority after 2021 peak-rain overload and documents buffers, underground storage, extra rainwater sewers and neighbourhood interventions. The municipality reports almost 11,000 drains. Policy, inventory and completed works do not establish event-time surface/sewer condition, capacity or drainage rate; no standard reuse licence is stated for these pages/documents.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Landgraaf / Staatstoezicht op de Mijnen
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Former coal mining, rising mine water and post-closure ground effects
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal claims page current in 2026; SodM sector state and November 2025 Kerkrade Mijnwater advice inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality states that pumping stopped after mine closure and rising mine water caused ground movement and sometimes housing damage such as wall cracks. I3ML began phased online claims on 22 December 2025 and opened a physical Heerlen desk on 2 January 2026.

SodM distinguishes gradual uplift after pumping stopped, local subsidence, occasional sinkholes above shallow workings, changing groundwater, mine-gas/deep-water-quality pathways and naturally active faults. These mechanisms are not interchangeable with one generic earthquake pulse.

SodM treats post-coal-mining care as a multi-decade risk-management task involving national government, province, municipalities, safety region, water board and water companies. Public pages do not provide parcel-level susceptibility, current movement, building damage, mine-water level or event probability.

Claims and sector evidence are static/historical and monitoring context, not a current damaging event. Exact source licensing for the page/document was not stated; provenance, publication/retrieval time, spatial coverage and uncertainty must be retained.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Provinciaal Risicoprofiel Limburg 2023–2027, cross-border cooperation and 2026 high-water planning
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile 2023–2027, effective 1 January 2024; draft Rampbestrijdingsplan Hoogwater Limburg 2026–2029 consultation announced 16 July 2026
supports: The official profile makes Euregional cooperation a central success factor and covers direct cross-border effects. Regional agreements include Kreis Heinsberg, Städteregion Aachen, Stadt Aachen and other German/Belgian partners; EMRIC last updated the non-public/on-request hazardous-facility inventory on 28 March 2023.

The profile separately classifies failure of electricity, gas, drinking water, wastewater, voice/data and oil, plus rail and road incidents and foreign health/security effects. Agreement existence does not establish scenario-time units, travel time, availability, language/interoperability or resource commitment.

The current high-water-plan consultation explicitly distinguishes the regional water system, the Maas, and defence failure/polder effects and uses water-board inundation maps, high-water messages and water pictures for decisions. Landgraaf's Worm/dry-valley problem must not be silently mapped to a generic major-river event.
The profile and planning announcement are official scenario/governance evidence, not a forecast or operational order; no machine incident feed or standard reuse licence is supplied by the pages.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — NWB national road graph, Landgraaf station and cross-border Aachen rail context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail public station/track snapshot retrieved 3 September; OVapi GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB supplies only two GM0882 scenario links: N300 to Kerkrade and N300 to Brunssum. Both carry nominal 150 scenario units, belong to one physical N300 corridor and support mobility/supply only; they are not two independent measured capacities.

ProRail places station Landgraaf inside GM0882. The line splits toward Kerkrade and Herzogenrath; the 6.5 km Landgraaf–Herzogenrath section was electrified for direct services toward Aachen and contains a voltage-system interface. Official capacity analysis describes the border branch as single track with a strong gradient.

OVapi GTFS version 9543, under free-use/best-effort/no-SLA terms, supplies 43 stop areas assigned to GM0882 and an Arriva RE18 Liège–Aachen route. Timetable and stop presence do not establish incident operation, passenger counts, evacuation role, accessibility, power or replacement transport.

The scenario graph includes neither the German rail/road edge nor ordinary local streets and destinations. National graph truncation is NoData for cross-border connectivity, not evidence that only the N300 matters.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Public water assets, electricity planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Full-boundary assignment finds 31 HWH records: 28 weirs, one sewer pump and two wastewater works, SVI Abdissenbosch and RWZI Rimburg. HWH Kunstwerken is national/weekly and Waterketen DAMO contributor-dependent, both CC BY-SA 4.0. The small register count is not a complete sewer/topology inventory and does not establish telemetry, state, power, backup or restoration.

One NBNL postcode sample, 6374NJ, maps to Enexis Terwinselen: 156.9 MW existing and 116.8 MW required withdrawal, 58 MW/120-request withdrawal queue, 151.3 MW existing and 118.4 MW required injection, 44.9 MW/51-request injection queue, eleven projects and earliest year 2028. This at-least-quarterly/monthly planning sample is not municipality coverage, current load, outage or reserve; the publisher calls the product open data but no exact licence identifier was found.

RDI assigns 67 installations: 37 mobile, fifteen fixed-link, ten amateur, three broadcast and two other-mobile. Its WFS states no reuse licence or cadence. Daily attribution-licensed DUO data assigns fifteen education locations: ten primary, three secondary and two other. Points do not prove radio coverage, occupancy, shelter role, backup or operation.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 assigns no emergency department inside GM0882. Zuyderland Heerlen is nearest at 6.54 km straight-line and reports 24/7 emergency/acute-obstetric care, 24 rooms and 38,500 visits in 2025. Questionnaire values are not route time, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, generator endurance or guaranteed incident capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Cross-border drinking water, Terwinselen grid planning and Rimburg wastewater renovation
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator pages inspected 3 September 2026; RWZI Rimburg renovation marked completed 30 July 2026; Enexis Terwinselen study started 17 February 2026
supports: WML states that most of Landgraaf receives deep groundwater from Schinveld, while the southernmost area receives very soft German water bought from enwor and originating in the Eifel. It separately identifies the Schinveld source/groundwater-protection area, which extends into Germany. Source context does not expose pressure zones, storage, live quality, outage or restoration.

Enexis reports structural injection congestion through 2029 in parts of Kerkrade and Landgraaf supplied by Terwinselen MST Netdeel 1 and is preparing cable/substation reinforcement at Groenstraat through early 2028. Planning congestion and works are not an outage, feeder topology, emergency spare capacity or repair promise.

Waterschap Limburg marks the phased Rimburg wastewater renovation complete in July 2026; the sole treatment tank required a temporary installation during works, the electrical system and buffers were renewed, and the project involved Landgraaf and Kerkrade. Completion/design context does not establish current inflow, treatment margin, backup, downstream quality or incident state.

The operator pages do not state a standard dataset reuse licence or machine incident contract. Safe use requires publisher, issue/effective time, service-zone coverage, units, state class, uncertainty, security review and explicit NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — First-72-hour preparedness, support-point pilot, dependent-person transport and changing occupancy
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal guidance and March–July 2026 emergency-support-point pilot reports inspected 3 September 2026; event policy 2021
supports: Municipal guidance asks households to plan for the first 72 hours without ordinary services, identify people needing extra help and use the Zuidlimburgveilig app; cached advice remains available offline. Guidance is not measured preparedness, supplies or communications availability.

Landgraaf joined the 2026 pilot for physical emergency support points during simultaneous electricity, internet and telephony failure. The municipality says these points provide information and accept emergency reports but are not shelters; locations, staffing, equipment, activation and communication are being tested and are not published as a ready capacity layer.

The municipality's crisis page calls for sheltering indoors and switching off ventilation when instructed, police-directed evacuation, reception centres or friends/family, and institution-arranged special transport for dependent people, older residents and pupils. It publishes no event-valid destination, capacity, vehicle, route or verification state.

Municipal event policy allows Megaland and surroundings up to 70,000 visitors per day. This static maximum is neither an event calendar nor actual attendance, but proves that resident-only exposure can be materially incomplete. No standard reuse licence is stated for the pages/policy.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Timestamped weather/air context and nature-fire response limits
evidenceSources.edition: VRZL field exercise 8 June 2026; deployment observations valid 2 September 2026
supports: No KNMI weather or RIVM PM2.5 station lies inside GM0882. Maastricht Airport is the nearest KNMI point at 19.52 km and observed 17.4°C, 5.71 m/s gust and zero hourly rain at 23:30Z on 2 September; Heerlen-Jamboreepad is the nearest PM2.5 point at 3.95 km and observed 3.33 µg/m³ at 17:00Z. These external points are timestamped context, not municipal surfaces or forecasts.

KNMI observations are ten-minute CC BY 4.0 and RIVM air observations are hourly indicative data with no standard licence stated in the feed; missing local stations and null variables remain Unknown, not zero weather, heat, smoke or pollution.

VRZL trained 4x4 response on sand, mud and slopes because ordinary appliances cannot reach all nature-area locations, citing Brunssummerheide. This supports a terrain/access mechanism, not a fire perimeter, probability, response time or guaranteed resource.

Wildfire direct flame/affected zero and smoke-only outputs are narrow synthetic preset results. Without a selected ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture surface, wind forecast and German/Dutch access plan they are neither a local forecast nor an all-clear.

identity.summary: GM0882, Landgraaf, Limburg and safety region Limburg-Zuid agree across generated and official 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature id, code/name, province, safety-region membership and 2025 boundary/statistics editions agree.
The municipality reference point lies inside the generalized and full boundary.
No identity, province, safety-region or headline-population contradiction was found.

notes: The full 2025 CBS feature has 877 coordinate positions versus 90 in the app overview.
All 27 neighbourhoods, the single BAG place and seven BRT labels carry GM0882 coherently.
Terrain, flow paths, water-conveying roads, sewers, mine workings, German catchment/roads, buildings and assets cannot be inferred from a municipal centre or generalized polygon.

demography.summary: Official resident controls reconcile, but a very old population and large permitted event crowds make static residents an incomplete incident exposure denominator.
notes: Official population is 36,839, households 17,769, density 1,499/km², age 65+ 28.2% and one-person households 6,608.
Neighbourhood rows sum to 36,820 (-19, -0.052%); households sum to 17,765 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 10,405.

Megaland policy permits up to 70,000 visitors per day, while schools, rail, recreation, care, workers and German cross-border movement also change people present. No incident occupancy feed is consumed.

regionalDetail.summary: Neighbourhood detail is useful, but the model does not consume source-versioned runoff, sewer, groundwater, mine, utility or facility state.
notes: Core demographic fields cover 27/27 neighbourhoods; several housing/access fields are partial and district heat/charging are entirely absent. Null is not imputed.

Official sources identify local dry-valley runoff, mixed sewers, water-conveying roads, mine-water effects and cross-border supply, but their governing spatial/temporal datasets are not connected to the scenario clock.
HWH, NBNL, RDI, DUO, RIVM, WML, Enexis, KNMI and operator pages remain context-only and effectsSimulation=false without live continuity evidence.

settlements.summary: The one BAG place and seven BRT labels coherently represent Landgraaf's principal cores and Rimburg border community.
notes: BAG designates Landgraaf; BRT adds named cores and Rimburg/Op de Hoven orientation.
No place-centre mismatch was found.
Labels do not establish people present, runoff catchments, mine susceptibility, service continuity, evacuation zones or hazard footprints.

transport.summary: The N300 and station are traceable, but the national scenario graph truncates German connections and omits event-valid local/care access.
notes: Two N300 edges to Kerkrade and Brunssum belong to one physical corridor; nominal 150 values are non-additive scenario units, not throughput.
Station Landgraaf and scheduled RE18 connect toward Herzogenrath/Aachen, but rail does not affect mobility or supply and no German road/mutual-aid edge exists in the scenario graph.
No selected runoff/flood/fire/ground event, ordinary street, closure, rail power/interface, replacement bus, emergency destination, occupancy or measured capacity controls access.
Zuyderland Heerlen is external and 6.54 km straight-line away; that is not event-time travel, acceptance or guaranteed access.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong local water, mining, cross-border and 72-hour planning evidence exists, but no live event, asset state or accountable action is consumed.
notes: Official evidence supports steep-runoff/sewer/Worm flooding, post-mining ground pathways, cross-border rail/water/mutual aid, nature access limits and a high vulnerable-person share.
Operator/project data retain publication/retrieval time and limited coverage and cannot be silently aligned to canonical T+0.
Preparedness and support-point pilots exist, but actual household readiness, point locations, shelter/care capacity, vulnerable transport, German resources and event occupancy remain Unknown.
Rainfall, groundwater, mine, watercourse, sewer, wastewater, power, drinking-water, gas, telecom, road/rail, facility, industrial and restoration states remain Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical scenarios execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0882 pnpm audit:model passed two tests covering ten presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/facilities/supply.
Focused inline Vite SSR inspection captured each preset at T+24/T+72 and full river, pluvial and compound trajectories without creating a repository scratch file.

Earthquake direct ground forcing becomes exact zero by T+12; wildfire has zero flame/affected but smoke/drought forcing; coastal has zero direct water but indirect wind stress; cyber has no selected target.
Outputs are deterministic exercise indices and resident-equivalents, not observations, probabilities, casualties, measured depths, asset/route states or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation, causal ledgers and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All service availability stays in [0,1]; hazards, demand, delivery, affected residents and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero intensity returns exact zero event hazard, affected population and attributable burden; repeated runs are deterministic and burden is monotone.
Every service allocates all 27 neighbourhoods and reconciles to 36,839 residents; local demand/delivery closes and layer selection does not mutate the scenario.
Passing arithmetic does not validate major-river eligibility, runoff depth, mine mechanism, German topology, occupancy, route feasibility or restoration precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A persistent major-river scalar and common neighbourhood seed conflict with Landgraaf's dry-valley/Worm, mining, heat, fire and cyber mechanisms.
notes: River depth reaches exactly 1.159687 m by T+12 and remains unchanged through T+72 without a selected major river, Worm hydrograph, rainfall/terrain run, defence, connected footprint, arrival or recession.
At T+24 nearly every active hazard ranks Lauradorp, Waubach, Heistraat, Exdel and Rimburg first in the same order; compound only swaps Heistraat to first. Heat and cyber also reuse this sequence.

Rimburg is officially exposed to runoff/Worm mechanisms, while mine effects follow workings/faults and fire follows vegetation/access. Occasional agreement for one neighbourhood cannot validate a shared all-hazard seed.
A common seed cannot substitute for elevation/flow paths, sewer/catchment, mine-workings/deformation, heat/shade, fuel/moisture, plume/source/target, buildings, activity or exposed-object geometry.

serviceDependencies.summary: Logical N300 links remain separate from utilities, but cross-border water/rail/mutual aid, wastewater, care, communications and facility dependencies are absent or synthetic.
notes: N300 links support mobility/supply only, avoiding false road-derived utility topology, but no German roads/rail, local streets, selected closures, destinations or measured capacities govern response.
Thirty-one HWH records, two wastewater works and almost 11,000 municipal drains do not form an approved runoff–sewer–pump–RWZI graph and do not causally influence drainage/water recovery.

WML's German/southern and Schinveld source facts, Enexis/NBNL planning, 67 antennas, fifteen schools and external acute care supply no incident-time topology, occupancy, priority, backup or restoration.
Exact service percentages remain transparent synthetic indices pending safe aggregate authority/operator/facility calibration.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers close, but local event selection, evidence time, cross-border coordination and accountable first-72-hour actions remain outside the graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipal pressure contributions reconcile exactly.
Public layers correctly remain affectsSimulation=false; trace does not select rainfall/runoff, Worm, mine movement, road/rail, utility, RWZI, care, facility, occupancy or German mutual-aid state.

Required decisions include warning/shelter/evacuation, water-conveying-road closure, sewer/RWZI and mine monitoring, German liaison/resource requests, acute-care referral, vulnerable transport, support-point activation and re-entry.
Actions lack accountable owner, trigger, request/acknowledgement, decision, resource, dependency, execution, verification and rollback states.

recovery72h.summary: Exact river/compound plateaus and rapid pluvial clearing have no Landgraaf authority, operator or milestone calibration.
notes: River T+72 retains exactly 1.159687 m, severity 0.363191, pressure 0.397107, 13,344 affected and 1,018,940.815 deprived person-hours; most service values are unchanged after T+24 while facilities falls from 0.612921 to 0.452845.
Compound T+72 retains exactly 0.523322 m, pressure 0.529731, 20,228 affected and 1,387,836.474 person-hours; most services plateau after T+24 while facilities declines.
Pluvial depth and affected residents become exact zero at T+48 and the status is operational at T+72 despite official ongoing work on terrain, dry-valley, sewer and Worm interactions.
Keep conservative disruption as an exercise guard, expose uncertainty and do not imply local clearance, treatment, access, utility, care or German-support promises until milestone owners verify them.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, place and demographic controls reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM0882, Landgraaf, Limburg and Limburg-Zuid agree; the centre and all place/neighbourhood records are coherent. CBS reports 36,839 residents and neighbourhood rows differ by -19 (-0.052%).
findings.action: Retain source editions, licence, suppression/null semantics and published-versus-allocated reconciliation without rewriting rounded observations.

findings.summary: Sparse fields, absent local observations and truncated cross-border coverage remain Unknown rather than false zero or safety.
findings.evidence: District heat/charging, provider topology/state, local acute-care/weather/air points, German road/mutual-aid state and incident occupancy are absent. One NBNL sample and public register points are not complete coverage.
findings.action: Keep source coverage, retrieval/effective time, edition, licence, quality, suppression and NoData through ingestion, aggregation, simulation eligibility and UI; distinguish scoped observed zero from Unknown.

findings.summary: A generic major-river scalar emits an unsupported exact 1.159687 m flood through T+72.
findings.evidence: Depth reaches 1.159687 m at T+12 and stays exact through T+72 with 13,344 affected and 1,018,940.815 person-hours. Official evidence instead identifies the Worm regional stream, steep dry valleys, water-conveying roads and sewer overload; no hydrograph, rainfall/terrain run, defence, footprint, arrival, probability or recession is selected.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing river depth, exposure and recovery until Waterschap Limburg/VRZL select a versioned Worm or runoff event. Retain the scalar only as a non-operational diagnostic and preserve unmodelled cells as Unknown, not dry.

findings.summary: Dry-valley runoff, water-conveying roads, mixed sewers and groundwater are absent from pluvial allocation and recovery.
findings.evidence: Rimburgerweg/Lindegracht convey extreme runoff from higher urban/rural land through dry valleys to Rimburg/Worm, and properties fail the provincial waterlogging standard. The model emits 0.506896 m at T+24, then exact zero depth/affected at T+48 and operational T+72 without a hyetograph, elevation/flow grid, intervention edition, sewer state, soil saturation or groundwater condition.
findings.action: Ingest the governing Water in Balans/stress-test/runoff-sewer surfaces with rainfall, terrain, infiltration/groundwater, intervention, units, cells, uncertainty and NoData. Do not infer rapid clearing from preset time alone.

findings.summary: The earthquake preset cannot represent post-coal-mining uplift, subsidence, groundwater change or sinkholes.
findings.evidence: Earthquake forcing is only 0.001231 at T+6 and exact zero after T+12. Municipality/SodM evidence identifies slowly rising mine water, differential movement, local subsidence, occasional sinkholes, groundwater and mine-gas/water-quality pathways; none is selected or spatially tied to workings, faults, buildings or observations.
findings.action: Create a separately named, authority-reviewed post-mining ground scenario/context layer with monitoring edition and mechanism-specific uncertainty. Never relabel gradual mine effects as earthquake or treat a zero earthquake pulse as stable ground.

findings.summary: Nearly every unrelated active T+24 hazard reuses the same five-neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire rank Lauradorp, Waubach, Heistraat, Exdel and Rimburg first in that order; compound merely moves Heistraat to first. Local runoff, mining, heat, vegetation/fire, plume and cyber target mechanisms require different evidence surfaces.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with hazard-specific physical surfaces and source/target/exposed-object intersections. Preserve deterministic ties only after evidence-derived values; unsupported cells stay Unknown rather than pseudo-precise.

findings.summary: German cross-border transport, catchment, drinking-water and mutual-aid dependencies are missing from the causal graph.
findings.evidence: The scenario has only two N300 links to Dutch neighbours. Official evidence identifies the single-track Landgraaf–Herzogenrath/Aachen railway and voltage interface, a Worm catchment rising in Aachen, formal Kreis Heinsberg/Städteregion Aachen/City Aachen cooperation, and enwor/Eifel drinking water for southern Landgraaf. None affects access, water or response.
findings.action: Add safe aggregate German interface nodes with source/valid time, physical mode, direction, authority/owner, request/acknowledgement state, availability and Unknown capacity; do not invent foreign topology or mutual-aid delivery.

findings.summary: Runoff, sewer, RWZI, source-water and power dependencies are visible but non-causal.
findings.evidence: HWH assigns 28 weirs, one sewer pump and two wastewater works while the municipality reports almost 11,000 drains and multiple storage/sewer interventions. RWZI Rimburg has one treatment tank and renewed electrical/buffer systems; WML uses Schinveld plus German water. No approved connectivity, compatible capacity, live state, quality, power/backup or restoration affects water/drainage.
findings.action: Build a Waterschap/municipality/WML-approved non-sensitive runoff–sewer–pump–RWZI/source-zone graph with event-valid state and backup bands; keep inventories, design status and missing connections non-causal and Unknown.

findings.summary: External acute care, vulnerable transport, support points and event crowds cannot alter first-72-hour priorities.
findings.evidence: Age 65+ is 28.2%; no emergency department lies inside GM0882 and Zuyderland Heerlen is 6.54 km straight-line away. Fifteen schools and 67 antennas lack occupancy/continuity, support-point roles remain a pilot, and Megaland permits up to 70,000 visitors per day. The model uses 36,839 static residents and no care/referral/transport/visitor state.
findings.action: Add authorised non-sensitive facility roles, referral/access bands, vulnerable-person assistance, support-point activation and time-varying occupancy/event calendars; staffing, beds, vehicles, crowds, coverage and backup remain Unknown unless supplied.

findings.summary: Zero local flame is a narrow preset result, not an all-clear for cross-border nature fire or smoke.
findings.evidence: Wildfire has zero flame and affected residents but non-zero smoke/drought forcing. VRZL identifies sand, mud, slopes and ordinary-appliance access limits around Brunssummerheide, while the municipality borders linked German/Dutch nature. No ignition, perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind, plume or cross-border access/resource state is selected.
findings.action: Retain the synthetic/direct-versus-indirect label. Add a local exercise only with authority-approved ignition/perimeter, fuel/weather, access, plume, protective-action and uncertainty evidence; missing fire cells remain Unknown, not safe.

findings.summary: Exact flood/service plateaus and rapid pluvial clearing have no local milestone contract.
findings.evidence: River depth stays 1.159687 m after T+12 and most services plateau after T+24; compound stays 0.523322 m through T+72. Conversely pluvial becomes direct-zero at T+48. No selected runoff/Worm event, sewer/RWZI inspection, road/rail access, utility state, German liaison, care state or verified restoration milestone supports these transitions.
findings.action: Replace exact transitions with evidence-classed uncertainty envelopes and owner-verified milestones for water exclusion/drainage, ground inspection, route access, utility isolation/repair, treatment, care/facility readiness and re-entry.

findings.summary: The complete numerical, checkpoint, allocation, ledger and recovery-accounting contract passes for GM0882.
findings.evidence: The mandatory gate covers ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/deterministic, zero intensity is exact, local/service totals reconcile, ledgers close, burden is monotone, road routes support mobility/supply only and layer selection is invariant.
findings.action: Keep GM0882 and national ALL coverage in regression; add regional-versus-major-river, pluvial recovery, mine-mechanism, border-interface, occupancy and Unknown-versus-zero assertions.

corrections.summary: Replace the generic GM0882 major-river scalar with authority-selected Worm regional-water and dry-valley runoff/sewer events.
corrections.validation: Use Waterschap Limburg Water in Balans/Worm data, municipal Watertakenplan/stress-test evidence, AHN/BRO where governing, and the full 877-position CBS 2025 boundary. Require a named regional-stream hydrograph or rainfall hyetograph/run, terrain/intervention edition, flow paths/water-conveying roads, soil saturation/infiltration/groundwater, sewer/surface assumptions, cells/CRS, units, issue/valid time, uncertainty, coverage, NoData and licence. Until selected, direct depth/exposure/recovery is Unknown; tests must reject generic major-river eligibility and automatic T+48 dryness.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic/runoff assessment, ground-stability statement, evacuation order, outage, route/rail guarantee or operator commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood sums need not equal the municipality control; null statistics, provider, capacity, monitoring, facility or forecast fields are Unknown, not zero.

The 90-position overview is suitable for display/selection, not terrain, dry-valley, sewer, groundwater, mine-workings, asset, building, road/rail or border intersection; use the full 877-position geometry.
The Worm is a German-border regional stream and local flood pathway; official project facts are not a selected hydrograph, rainfall run, defence state, connected footprint, probability or depth.
Water in Balans and Watertakenplan evidence identify known mechanisms and works, not live rainfall, surface/sewer capacity, soil saturation, groundwater, property depth or clearance time.
Mine claims and SodM sector evidence establish post-mining mechanisms but not current parcel susceptibility, movement, damage, mine-water level, sinkhole probability or a scenario-time event.
No KNMI weather or RIVM PM2.5 station is assigned inside GM0882; nearest external values are timestamped point context and no-match is not zero weather, heat, smoke or pollution.
HWH's 31 records and the municipal almost 11,000 drains are differently scoped inventories; neither establishes completeness, connectivity, state, capacity, power/backup or restoration.

The two N300 links are one physical corridor and nominal 150 values are scenario units; national topology omits German connections and ordinary local roads, so absent edges are NoData rather than no dependency.

Station/GTFS/ProRail records and formal Euregional agreements do not establish live train/road operation, passenger/resources, replacement transport, border interoperability, response time or mutual-aid delivery.
WML's Schinveld/German source facts, Enexis/NBNL planning and completed RWZI work do not establish pressure/feeder/sewer topology, live quality/load/state, backup or restoration.
No emergency department lies inside GM0882; Zuyderland questionnaire figures and straight-line distance do not prove route access, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, generator endurance or capacity.
RDI antenna and DUO education points do not establish communications coverage, building occupancy, shelter/support role, backup power, staffing or operation.
Emergency support points are a pilot and explicitly not shelters; published guidance supplies no event-valid location, activation, capacity, endurance, staffing or communications state.

Megaland's 70,000-visitors-per-day policy maximum is not a calendar or attendance observation; registered residents also exclude rail users, workers, pupils, care clients, recreation and cross-border visitors.
Direct coastal/fire/earthquake zero is a narrow model statement, not no indirect surge/supply, nature fire/smoke, seismic or post-mining ground risk.

Recovery after T+72, pre-impact lead time, German service/resource consequences, authorised shelters/care destinations, facility/household readiness and resource constraints remain outside locally validated scope.
